import sys, json

# The fence the block contract asks for, and the one this cell shipped first.
# ```sidecar carries ONE object whose TOP-LEVEL KEYS are the sections; ```memory
# is the single-section form and is read as the section `memory`, so a colony
# that has not been rewired yet keeps writing (GH #605).
#
# The grammar is a 1:1 port of the harness parser
# (`workshop/evals/conversation-guide/run_guide.py`): the grammar that MEASURED
# the sidecar and the grammar that CUTS it in production have to be one grammar,
# or the adoption number stops speaking for the shipped lane.
FENCE = "```sidecar"
LEGACY_FENCE = "```memory"
LEGACY_SECTION = "memory"
# What makes a bare ```json fence or a naked trailing object an ATTEMPT rather
# than a code block. They are shapes of the legacy `memory` section: the cell
# judges no section here, it only recognises a wrapper the model missed.
LEGACY_MARKERS = ('"facts"', '"nothing_new"')


def fenced(text, low, fence):
    """The span a fence claims: `(raw, start, end)`, or `("", -1, -1)`."""
    at = low.find(fence)
    if at < 0:
        return "", -1, -1
    head = text.find("\n", at)
    close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
    if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
        return text[head + 1:close], at, close + 3
    # The opener is there and the closer is not: the completion stopped inside
    # the block. The whole tail from the fence is the attempt -- falling through
    # to the naked-object probe below would cut the JSON and leave the bare
    # fence line standing in the answer, which is the same leak one character
    # smaller (GH #534).
    return (text[head + 1:] if head >= 0 else ""), at, len(text)


def find_block(text):
    """The sidecar an answer carries: `found`, `legacy`, `raw`, `stripped`.

    NOTHING here repairs or re-serialises what the model wrote, and NOTHING here
    knows a section: a splitter that fixed a block would hand its readers its own
    repair instead of the model's, and one that judged a section by name would
    make every new section a change to this cell (GH #605). The only tolerance is
    on the FENCE, because decorating the wrapper is the failure mode
    format-restricted instructions actually show.

    `stripped` is computed whether or not the JSON in the middle parses, and that
    is the retraction GH #534 wrote here: `found` alone decides that the fence
    leaves the answer, because the cut is the span this function already located
    and the prose either side of it is the same prose either way.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence, legacy in ((FENCE, False), (LEGACY_FENCE, True)):
        raw, start, end = fenced(text, low, fence)
        if start >= 0:
            return {"found": True, "legacy": legacy, "raw": raw,
                    "stripped": (text[:start] + text[end:]).strip()}
    # A bare ```/```json fence whose body carries a legacy payload counts as an
    # attempt: the model produced it and missed the label.
    for opener in ("```json", "```"):
        probe = 0
        while True:
            at = low.find(opener, probe)
            if at < 0:
                break
            head = text.find("\n", at)
            close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
            if head < 0 or close < 0:
                break
            body = text[head + 1:close]
            if any(m in body for m in LEGACY_MARKERS):
                return {"found": True, "legacy": True, "raw": body,
                        "stripped": (text[:at] + text[close + 3:]).strip()}
            probe = close + 3
    # A naked object at the end of the answer, same reasoning. Scanned from the
    # LAST opening brace backwards: the payload nests (`topic` is an object), so
    # the last brace in the text is an inner one and a lone rfind would never see
    # a real payload here.
    brace = text.rfind("{")
    while brace >= 0:
        tail = text[brace:]
        if any(m in tail for m in LEGACY_MARKERS):
            return {"found": True, "legacy": True, "raw": tail,
                    "stripped": text[:brace].strip()}
        brace = text.rfind("{", 0, brace)
    return {"found": False, "legacy": False, "raw": "", "stripped": text}


doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
h = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = dict(h.get("hop") or {})
msgs = d.get("messages") or []


def emit_pass_through(extra=None):
    """Form 1: the turn travels on exactly as it arrived."""
    header = dict(hop)
    if extra:
        header.update(extra)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"header": header, "messages": msgs}))


# A round with tool calls belongs to the dispatcher, whole. The splitter only
# ever touches a plain answer completion -- building the mixed form (text beside
# an async call in one message) is exactly the shape that strands a round
# (GH #378), and this is where we walk around it rather than into it.
if any(isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("type") == "tool_call" for m in msgs):
    emit_pass_through()
    sys.exit(0)

# The LAST text turn that carries a block is the one that carries the sidecar:
# a model that quoted a fence earlier in the same completion did not annotate
# twice, it annotated at the end.
found_at, ann = -1, None
for i, m in enumerate(msgs):
    if not isinstance(m, dict):
        continue
    text = m.get("text")
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text:
        continue
    probe = find_block(text)
    if probe["found"]:
        found_at, ann = i, probe

if ann is None:
    emit_pass_through()
    sys.exit(0)

# Found decides the cut, readable decides the lane: the block comes out of the
# answer in every case from here on.
cleaned = list(msgs)
turn = dict(msgs[found_at])
turn["text"] = ann["stripped"]
cleaned[found_at] = turn

try:
    parsed = json.loads(ann["raw"].strip())
except ValueError:
    parsed = None
if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
    parsed = None

if parsed is None:
    # The block is there and unreadable, and it STILL leaves the answer.
    #
    # RETRACTED (GH #534), because it was measured in a running colony: this
    # branch used to pass the answer through untouched, fence included, on the
    # reasoning that half-cutting a block nobody can read corrupts the answer
    # for the sake of a write that cannot happen anyway. A model dropped one
    # closing brace and a person read the JSON in their chat window. There is no
    # half cut to fear -- the span was already located, the prose either side of
    # it is the same prose -- so the only thing that branch bought was the leak.
    #
    # What does not change is the refusal to repair: nothing is re-serialised
    # and NOTHING goes out on `sidecar`, because there is nothing readable to
    # hand a reader. The flag stays, so the close pass can still tell "the model
    # missed the form" from "the model never annotated" and still owes the turn
    # an extraction.
    header = dict(hop)
    header["sidecar"] = "malformed"
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"header": header, "messages": cleaned}))
    sys.exit(0)

# One object, one message per top-level key. The cell distributes nothing and
# recognises nothing: `hop.section` is what the edges downstream read, so a
# section this tree has never heard of travels without a line of code here.
sections = {LEGACY_SECTION: parsed} if ann["legacy"] else parsed
out, dropped = [], []
for key, payload in sections.items():
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        # A section is an OBJECT. A string or a list under a top-level key is a
        # model that wrote past the form, and there is no body to carry it in --
        # it is dropped with its name on the record rather than guessed at.
        dropped.append(key)
        continue
    out.append({"header": {"route": "sidecar", "section": key},
                "messages": [], "section": key, "payload": payload})

answer = {"finish_reason": "stop"}
if dropped:
    answer["sidecar_dropped"] = ",".join(dropped)
emitted = [{"header": answer, "messages": cleaned}] + out
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(emitted if len(emitted) > 1 else emitted[0]))

description.purpose: The seam that takes the sidecar back out of an answer, and it knows no section. A brain completion arrives on the answer path; if its text carries a fenced `sidecar` block, ONE JSON object is read out of it and ONE MESSAGE PER TOP-LEVEL KEY leaves on route `sidecar` with `hop.section` set to that key, beside the answer with the block cut out. The legacy single-section fence `memory` is still read and becomes the section `memory`, so a colony that has not been rewired keeps writing. Without a block contract in the brain's instructions there is nothing to find and this cell is a pure pass-through.
description.use_when: Inside the talky composite, on the brain's answer path only -- between ./brain and ./dispatcher. The parent MUST wire the `sidecar` port out of the composite and distribute it on `hop.section`, or every section dead-letters while the answers keep going out fine, which is the failure nobody sees.
description.not_in_scope: No repair, no re-serialisation, no receiver knowledge. The cell never judges a section by name: what a section means belongs to whoever declared it, and a splitter that knew the names would need changing for every new one. A block that does not parse, or whose top level is not an object, is CUT out of the answer like any other and then dropped -- only the flag travels, and nothing unreadable is handed on, because a repaired block would be this cell's invention rather than the model's. RETRACTED in GH #534: until then such a block was left INSIDE the answer, and a model that dropped one closing brace put raw JSON in front of a person. Found decides the cut; readable decides the lane. A section whose value is not an object is dropped by name rather than guessed at. No tool-call round is ever touched: a completion carrying calls belongs to the dispatcher whole, because the mixed form -- text beside an async call in one message -- is the shape that strands a round (GH #378) and this cell exists to walk around it.
description.emits_meaning: route sidecar: one message per section the block carried, `hop.section` naming it, body `{messages: [], section, payload}` -- the payload is the section object as the model wrote it, parsed and not otherwise touched. On the answer half: finish_reason stop, and the same turns minus the fence; `sidecar_dropped` lists the sections that were not objects, comma-separated, in the order the model wrote them. sidecar malformed on a single message: a block was there and could not be read, so it was cut out of the answer and went nowhere -- the reader never sees a fence this cell found, and the close pass still owes the turn an extraction (GH #534).
description.consumes_meaning: the brain's completion on stop or tool_calls (messages plus the hop it arrived with). The fence grammar is a 1:1 port of the harness parser that measured the adoption of this form (```sidecar, the legacy ```memory, plus a tolerance for a bare ```json fence or a naked trailing object carrying the legacy payload): the grammar that measured it and the grammar that cuts it are one grammar.
examples: answer + ```sidecar block with two sections -> three messages: prose to the dispatcher, one message per section on route sidecar
answer + legacy ```memory block -> two messages: prose to the dispatcher, the block as section memory
answer with no block -> one message, byte-identical (a colony without the block contract)
tool-call round -> one message, byte-identical, block or no block
